授業目的: This course takes advantage of KGU‘s proximity to Kobe City (population 1.4 m) to introduce students to the history of this modern city as well as related themes in the historical of Japan at large. The course will provide students with basic facts, concepts, and perspectives for their independent, active exploration of the city’s past and present against the backdrop of the standard textbook story of the nation. This course consists of lectures, quizzes, field trips, reflections, and a final presentation.
到達目標: By introducing concepts and facts speciMically relevant to Kobe, this course aims to help students acquire a basic understanding of this international metropolis at the university’s doorstep. Through learning about Kobe, this course also seeks to shed light on general questions relating to Japan’s recent past as well as present conditions from multiple perspectives, including the political, economic, cultural, social, and environmental. After taking this course, students will have a broad understanding not only of Kobe but also, through the example of Kobe, the country as a whole. This course will compliment as well as extend what other general courses on Japan offer.
授業方法: Face-to-face classes including lectures, presentations, and field trips.

教科書/Required texts0: All readings will be announced in class and provided online free.
